The polar l-one computation independently confirms the comparison. value.rationale: The stability of Euclidean clipping for coordinatewise-bounded noise is naturally motivated by epigraphical splitting and weighted inverse problems. The exact arbitrary-weight coefficient has an O(n²) sorted-candidate evaluation, sharp strict contractivity rigidity, and a complete n+1-point classification of all worst weighting patterns. A rank-two eigenvalue law proves maximal instability scales as sqrt(n)/2 despite calibrated weights giving norm one, a structural and potentially useful design tradeoff not captured by ordinary Euclidean nonexpansivity.
